issues.description: The problem statement (top-level tasks) instructs students that dd_get_amplitude should "return the probability corresponding to the given bitstring as a float" (a real probability), while both the template dd_simulation.py and the solution implement/describe dd_get_amplitude as returning the amplitude (a complex number). This is a return-type / semantic mismatch: students reading the problem text will implement/expect a probability (float), but the template function and the reference solution operate with complex amplitudes. This discrepancy can confuse students and lead to incorrect implementations or failing tests.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the specification consistent with the template and solution. Either (A) change the problem statement to request that dd_get_amplitude return the complex amplitude for the given bitstring (and note that the measurement probability is |amplitude|^2), or (B) if the intent was to return a probability, update the template and solution to return a float probability (e.g., np.abs(amplitude)**2) and adjust all uses/tests accordingly. Option A is recommended because the template and reference solution already implement and use amplitudes.
